title: ARC chain not used to excuse DMARC failures — breaks mailing list delivery
description: auth.rs comments: 'a valid ARC chain should excuse DMARC failure for list mail, but that requires policy-level ARC bypass logic added in a later epic'. Scenario: high-volume mailing lists (Mailman, Listserv) that break DKIM but add ARC seals (Google Groups, Yahoo Groups, most large list providers). If the sending domain has DMARC policy=reject and the message transits a forwarder with ARC, the current code may reject valid list mail. A passing ARC chain is computed by verify_arc() but never checked against the DMARC reject decision. Maintenance consequence: operators will see legitimate mailing list mail rejected; they'll file bugs; you'll explain the ARC bypass is missing but they won't understand why it wasn't done at first. At minimum, document the limitation in the README/man page so operators know to expect it.
